transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sophie (Redwood SE), Aisha (Lyra CTO), Ravi (Lyra ML Eng), Claire (Lyra DevOps), Omar (Lyra Product)

Summary: quick discovery focused on PLG/self-serve Redwood API — customer curious about time-to-first-token, free credits, and when they'd need Dedicated / Private. Security/SSO and latency targets discussed.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we all have the agenda up, quick intro then figure out your goals for a quickstart — i'll hand over to sophie for a couple of technical notes after the intro.
[00:14] Aisha: yep thanks jordan, appreciate it. we are Lyra Dynamics, small infra team building conversational assistants inside our core product. trying to understand if we can get started with a hosted API, how soon we can ship, and what the lift to Dedicated or Private would be later.
[00:28] Jordan: perfect, that's exactly what we do. quick one-line: we offer a hosted api for fastest time-to-value, dedicated reserved capacity for predictable perf, and private for vpc/on-prem for compliance. for a lot of teams the quickstart path is hosted + free credits to prototype.
[00:42] Ravi: curious — what's time-to-first-token typically? like from signup to being able to hit an endpoint with a model that resembles production?
[00:49] Sophie: most teams can be up in under an hour — free account, get api key, we have SDKs and curl examples. you'll get sample prompts and a small eval harness. i'm thinking, realistically maybe 30–60 minutes for a simple chat flow. if you want to run benchmark latency tests or larger workloads it's a few hours to configure payloads.
[01:10] Claire: okay good. our constraints: latency under 300ms p95 for short prompts (<128 tokens), and costs need to be predictable. also we have strict data retention policy — logs must be deletable and we need audit trails.
[01:25] Jordan: got it. so two things — latency target is within the realm of hosted for many models, depending on model choice and region; we can also route to dedicated capacity if you need guaranteed p95. on retention: hosted supports configurable retention and we have enterprise controls for audit logs; for the highest controls your security team often goes Dedicated or Private.
[01:43] Aisha: and what's the difference operationally between Dedicated and Private? we may need SSO and our corporate KMS.
[01:51] Sophie: Dedicated = reserved GPU pools in our cloud offering, single-tenant performance and data isolation, you still use Redwood control plane. Private = customer-managed control plane, can be VPC peered or on-prem; more work to setup but you get customer KMS and fully managed audit logs within your network. SSO/SAML is supported both ways but Private gives you more direct network control.
[02:12] Omar: do you have a SOC2 / ISO attestation for hosted? our security team will want that before any PII touches the API.
[02:20] Jordan: yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO certs — happy to share the security pack and connect your compliance team. Sophie: i'll include the security pack link in the follow-up.
[02:31] Ravi: can you talk about pricing for quickstarts — free credits etc?
[02:35] Jordan: we usually give trial credits for self-serve signups; for PLG quickstarts we also have a credits program for proof-of-concept. i'll send the exact allocation and how to redeem. post-trial, pricing is usage-based per-token and per-embedding; Dedicated moves to a reserved capacity invoice.
[02:52] Claire: are there any gotchas with SDKs — we use python and node, hope the libraries are mature.
[02:58] Sophie: yep official SDKs for python, node, and a minimal go client. examples for streaming, function calling, and embeddings. sometimes transcription has little name mismatches — but overall folks find the SDKs easy for prototyping.
[03:12] Aisha: for our bench we want to test both accuracy and latency vs our current provider, and also a cost model. do you provide benchmarking guidance?
[03:20] Sophie: absolutely — we have a benchmark runbook. simplest path: give us a representative set of prompts and sample tokens, we'll run them on hosted and we can advise quantization/model choices. for strict latency we recommend trying smaller model variants and region selection. also we have KV/prefix caching suggestions to reduce token cost on repeated contexts.
[03:40] Ravi: on the hosted side, what's the SLA? do we get any uptime guarantees?
[03:44] Jordan: hosted has a baseline SLA for paid tiers; Dedicated has stronger SLA backing. For mission-critical we typically recommend Dedicated or Private with an SLA.
[03:53] Omar: curious about egress/data residency — any region options?
[03:56] Sophie: we run regions in NA, EU, and some APAC partners, you can pick region per request via routing. if you need specific residency in a country, Private or Dedicated with regional deployment is the right path.
[04:12] Aisha: security-wise the questions are SSO, KMS, logs, and is there any way to prevent model training on our data?
[04:19] Jordan: we don't train models on customer data; that's documented in the data handling policy. for Private deployments you can also keep everything inside your network and control keys.
[04:28] Claire: on onboarding — can we get a sandbox project with a preloaded sample so our PMs can demo quickly?
[04:33] Jordan: yes, we can provision a project with starter prompts and a sample app. i'll attach a quickstart repo link.
[04:42] Sophie: small technical note — when you move from prototyping to prod you can change quantization and batch sizing; those levers impact latency and cost and we help with recommendations in Redwood Optimize.
[04:57] Ravi: are there examples of customers who started on hosted and moved to Dedicated? curious about migration friction.
[05:03] Jordan: yeah multiple — typical pattern: prototype on hosted, then as traffic and SLOs need tightening they reserve capacity and migrate with minimal code changes — it's mostly a config and routing change rather than massive re-architecture.
[05:16] Omar: any competitors we should know about? we currently use openai for some features and looking at Anthropic for safety focused models.
[05:23] Sophie: yup those are common. we sometimes get compared on model catalog breadth and latency/cost. we emphasize production controls and predictable economics.
[05:35] Aisha: what would you need from us to get the free credits and sandbox?
[05:39] Jordan: just an email to link to the team and we'll provision. if you want a dedicated trial capacity for benchmarking that might be a short contract but we can start hosted trial first.
[05:48] Ravi: on the technical benchmark — our target: 300ms p95 on 64–128 token prompts; can you run that on typical models?
[05:57] Sophie: we can run it on a few model variants. for 300ms p95 you may need smaller models or dedicated routing; we'll test in-region and share results.
[06:07] Claire: do you support VPC peering for Private?
[06:10] Sophie: yes VPC peering and customer-managed VMs for on-prem packages.
[06:14] Jordan: i'll recap next steps at the end. any other big blockers?
[06:18] Aisha: our procurement is going to want a ballpark cost for a month of production traffic — is that something you can provide with some assumptions?
[06:25] Jordan: yes, if you share expected tokens per month and concurrency we can ballpark Hosted vs Dedicated costs. we'll ask for a short profile in the follow-up.
[06:35] Omar: one more question — do you have rate limits on the trial or throttles that would affect smoke testing?
[06:40] Sophie: trials have some soft rate limits to prevent abuse but they're typically high enough for functional tests; for load tests we can temporarily lift limits or set up a dedicated trial.
[06:50] Jordan: ok, quick recap and agreed next steps: jordan to send quickstart + credits link + security pack; sophie to run initial latency benchmark once customer shares payloads; customer to identify compliance contact and share token usage profile; schedule a follow-up tech demo after we have benchmark results.
[07:10] Aisha: thanks all, that sounds good — we'll get the sample prompts and compliance contact over the next few days.
[07:17] Jordan: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the links and a calendar invite for the next call.

End of transcript.
